name: Coldveil Operator's Full-Balaclava
description:
A close-fitting full balaclava in matte black and slate-grey paneling, constructed from a four-way stretch thermal-weave with a built-in PM2.5 filter layer across the mouth and nose zone. The face panel is reinforced with flat-bonded seams that don't bulk under a helmet or mask. Three port-access slits at the crown are sealed by magnetic flaps — open them and standard BCI jacks clear without removing the balaclava.

The rear panel has a wide occiput seam channel that accommodates basic spinal rig anchor plates. Sold through mid-tier tactical supply shops but popular with operatives, couriers, and anyone who needs to be anonymous in cold weather.
functionality: Thermal retention for sub-zero Shelf wind corridors. Integrated PM2.5 filtration handles acid-mist and industrial particulate. Magnetic crown flaps allow BCI port access without removal. Spinal rig channel prevents pressure points during extended wear with back-mounted augmentation.
what_it_says: You operate in conditions most people avoid, and you've thought through every piece of your kit.
story_hooks: A batch of Coldveil balaclavas was recalled quietly after the magnetic port-access flaps were found to interfere with a specific Axiom BCI model, causing momentary signal dropout — someone used that window to commit a crime.
A courier was identified by the specific wear pattern on their Coldveil's nose bridge — the only evidence in a high-profile theft case.
The filter membrane in older Coldveil units can be chemically treated to selectively block certain aerosolized compounds, a technique known only to a few Shelf chemists.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, form-fitting full-face covering that hugs the skull and neck contours. Matte black dominates the front and sides with slate-grey paneling along the crown and occiput, creating a geometric, tactical aesthetic. The weave catches minimal light—deliberately non-reflective. Appears almost featureless from distance, like a void where a face should be.
physical_description.fit: Second-skin compression fit; the four-way stretch thermal-weave conforms tightly to facial geometry without bunching. Sits snug against the jawline, cheekbones, and temples. The rear panel extends down to mid-cervical, allowing integration with spinal rigs without gaps.
physical_description.primary_material: Four-way stretch thermal-weave synthetic blend (heat-retention, moisture-wicking core) with integrated PM2.5 filter layer in the mouth-nose zone. Flat-bonded seams throughout—no raised stitching.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, slightly ribbed matte finish on the black sections. The grey panels show a finer weave texture. The PM2.5 filter zone is subtly quilted for durability. Overall: utilitarian, non-glossy, designed to remain tactile even in sub-zero conditions.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte black primary (face, front neck); slate-grey secondary (crown panels, occiput channel). No logos visible; branding is a small woven tag at the rear neckline. Zero reflectivity.
physical_description.closures: Magnetic flaps seal the three crown port-access slits; friction-fit neck opening with optional elastic closure strap (removable). No zippers or buckles—designed for quick BCI access.
distinctive_features: Three magnetic port-access slits at crown—allows BCI jack insertion without removal
Wide occiput seam channel for spinal rig anchor-plate accommodation
Flat-bonded seams—zero bulk under helmet or secondary mask layer
Thermal-weave maintains insulation while remaining thin enough for stacking
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional—mid-grade tactical apparel. Priced Φ180–240 through mid-tier suppliers. Not corpo luxury (no smart-fiber, no HUD integration), but above salvage-tier anonymous wear.
physical_description.cultural_context: Operatives, couriers, street runners, security personnel, corpo contractors, and anyone requiring anonymity + thermal protection. Worn by people who move through the GLMZ's colder zones (late autumn–spring) without drawing attention. Popular in ungoverned districts and corpo logistics chains.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in after 3–4 weeks: minor pilling on high-friction zones (jawline, neck), possible slight discoloration around the filter layer from repeated breathing/condensation. Long-term wear shows wear-shine on crown port seals and fading at pressure points. Well-maintained specimens remain nearly pristine.
